title: General Obligation Bonds to replace the current police facility
ballot_label: Caption: General Obligation Bonds to replace the current police facility. Question: Shall Forest Grove issue general obligation bonds not to exceed $29.5 million in principal for a new police facility? If the bonds are approved, they will be payable from taxes on property or property ownership that are not subject to the limits of sections 11 and 11b, Article XI of the Oregon Constitution.
summary: Forest Grove asks voters to authorize up to $29.5 million in general obligation bonds for a new police facility on city property at 19th and Birch. The city says its 1977 facility of 12,120 square feet has stayed the same size while the department grew from 12 to 42 personnel, and that remodeling or expanding it would cost more than building new.
yes_means: A yes vote authorizes Forest Grove to issue up to $29.5 million in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes, for a new police facility.
no_means: A no vote does not authorize the bonds, so the city would not issue them for a new police facility.
fiscal_impact: Principal not to exceed $29.5 million. Estimated levy rate $0.69 per $1,000 of assessed value, about $193 a year ($17 a month) for the average assessed home. Bonds may be issued in multiple series maturing in 21 years or less; actual rates may differ with interest rates and assessed values.

arguments.author: Henry Reimann, Forest Grove Police Chief
arguments.statement: In February 2026 legislative testimony seeking state funds for the project, Forest Grove Police Chief Henry Reimann says building a new police facility is the most cost-effective, operationally efficient, long-term solution.
arguments.excerpt: building a new facility is the most cost-effective, operationally efficient, and long-term solution.
